prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universally “best” HVAC company for everyone — the best choice depends on your exact location in Atlanta, your budget, the size/age of your home, ductwork condition, and whether you prioritize lowest price, longest warranty, or fastest scheduling. I can help you pick a great contractor — if you tell me your ZIP code and any preferences (budget, timeline, brand), I’ll find highly rated options and compare them.

Meanwhile, here’s a quick, practical guide to get the right company and avoid costly mistakes.

How to pick the best company
- Get at least 3 written estimates (same scope) so you can compare apples-to-apples.
- Verify license & insurance: Georgia requires an appropriate HVAC license and proof of general liability insurance and workers’ comp.
- Look for NATE-certified technicians and manufacturer training (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, etc.).
- Confirm they perform a Manual J load calculation (proper sizing) and will check/tell you about ductwork condition.
- Ask about labor and compressor warranties (manufacturer vs. installer warranty) and what’s included in the price (permits, removal/disposal, refrigerant recovery, baseline tune-up).
- Read recent Google, Yelp, and BBB reviews and ask for local references.

Questions to ask every contractor
1. Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide license number and COI?  
2. Will you do a Manual J load calculation and show me the results?  
3. What brand/models do you recommend and why? What SEER will I get?  
4. What is included in the written estimate? (permit, labor, materials, refrigerant, condensate lines, thermostats)  
5. What are the total warranties (unit, compressor, labor) and any conditions?  
6. Who does the work — company employees or subcontractors?  
7. How long will the job take and can you provide a written start date?  
8. Do you offer financing, rebates, or maintenance plans?  
9. Will you provide a copy of the permit and final inspection?  
10. What are your payment terms and do you accept credit?

Red flags
- Very low “too good to be true” price without a site visit.  
- No written estimate or contract.  
- Pressure to sign immediately or pay all cash up front.  
- Refusal to show license, insurance, or references.  
- No permit pulled for the job.

Typical price ranges (Atlanta, ballpark)
- Simple AC condenser-only replacement: roughly $3,500–$6,000.  
- Full system replacement (air handler + condenser + basic duct upgrades): $5,000–$10,000+.  
- High-efficiency or complex installations (ductwork, zoning, crawlspace difficulties): $8,000–$15,000+.  
Prices depend on home size, tonnage, SEER rating, and installation complexity.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated HVAC contractors near you (give me your ZIP).  
- Draft an email/phone script you can use to get comparable quotes.  
- Review 2–3 estimates and tell you which is the best value.

Which would you like to do next?
